clue.text: A Republican opponent's first sight of JFK?

parts.note: a rival is an opponent; the possessive supplies the final S

explanation.surface: A political sketch: what a Republican adversary of President Kennedy first saw of him.
explanation.walkthrough: JFK looks like the president, but it is New York's Kennedy airport, where the first thing a traveller sees is the arrivals hall.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport the incoming passengers' hall is the first part of the building a landing traveller sees.

clue.text: In truth, girl acts up OK, as some would have it

definitions.text: OK, as some would have it

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read bottom to top
In means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Honestly, the girl is behaving up and down fine, some say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as some would have it' warns that this spelling is non-standard; many insist on 'all right'.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-word spelling is a common informal variant meaning satisfactory or acceptable.

clue.text: Beer manufacture after initial loss adopts a way to be profitable

indicators.note: adopts means the brewing word takes the other pieces inside it
losing the initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: brewing is the making of beer
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Brewing that recovers from early losses finds a path to profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beer manufacture' reads as a phrase about brewing, but it is just the noun for the process, losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rewarding pays back in return, so it is profitable, financially or otherwise.

clue.text: Artist displaying front, ditch broadcast

parts.note: the van, as in vanguard, is the front

indicators.note: broadcast means heard spoken, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a dike is a ditch

explanation.surface: A painter putting on a show by announcing a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Van Dyck was a Flemish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Dyck was a seventeenth-century Flemish painter famous for his portraits of Charles I.

clue.text: On-line balance provided by lender

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales or balance
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An online bank balance supplied by a creditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On-line' looks like the internet word but splits: 'On' stacks the balance above the line in this down entry. 'provided by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A library lends books to its borrowers, so it is a lending institution.

clue.text: Wine producer's problem returning in the region of Central Austria

indicators.note: returning means the word for a problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
ca. (circa) means about or in the region of

indicators.note: central means take the middle letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A vintner's difficulty somewhere in the heart of Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'producer' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is a grape variety, so it is literally a producer of wine.

clue.text: Emperor maybe got to like his old clothes?

parts.note: the emperor is a species of moth, one example
eaten, as in what's eating you, means got to or upset

explanation.surface: Did the emperor take to his old wardrobe?
explanation.walkthrough: The Emperor seems a monarch, but it is a moth species, whose larvae chew clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn old clothes are full of holes chewed by larvae, which is exactly what the hyphenated adjective describes.

clue.text: It's posh, if contrived, one might plausibly argue

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smooth talking might claim it's posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophist is a person who uses clever but fallacious arguments that sound convincing.

clue.text: Being entirely self-centred overcomes resistance quickly

indicators.note: overcomes means the phrase covers or encloses the resistance letter

parts.note: being entirely self-centred is to be all ego
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Total egotism quickly beats any opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a lively, fast tempo.

clue.text: Maybe eight rupees due club possessing nothing

parts.note: money due is money owing

indicators.note: possessing means the club holds the zero inside it

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A money matter: rupees owed by a club that has nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eight' looks like a number but is a rowing crew's boat, hence 'Maybe', since an eight is one kind of craft propelled by oars.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing eight is an example of a boat moved by oars, flagged as such by 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Crush new seal perhaps, crossing line

indicators.note: crossing means the young seal straddles the line, holding it inside

parts.note: a newborn seal is called a pup, one example of such young animals

explanation.surface: An instruction to squash a newborn seal that has strayed over a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulp something is to crush it into a soft mass.

clue.text: Angry reminder to reform following grand political malpractice

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after the single letter

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: to reform means to reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irate memo calling for reform after a large-scale political scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerrymandering is named after US governor Elbridge Gerry, whose redrawn district looked like a salamander.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerrymandering is rigging electoral boundaries for party advantage, a classic abuse of political process.

clue.text: In fringes of teleplay, strains to get involved

indicators.note: In means the strained muscles go inside the fringe letters
fringes are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: to rick is to wrench or strain, so ricks means strains

explanation.surface: Actors on the edges of a TV drama straining to take part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link. The outer letters of 'teleplay' are T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricksy can mean intricate or complicated, the sense of involved as in a convoluted plot.

clue.text: Litter's about and makes one kind of cross

indicators.note: about means the litter word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to litter is to strew, so litters, written litter's, means strews

explanation.surface: A rubbish problem that makes a cross of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link. The St Andrew's cross is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The saltire, a diagonal cross, is named after Scotland's patron saint.

clue.text: Tip from Texas: this should stay on outside!

definitions.text: Tip from Texas: this should stay on outside!

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let the deleted text stand

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, so take the first letter of Texas

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice from the Lone Star State: keep this on when out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the hat: a Texan's headgear, which stays on outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brimmed cowboy hat associated with Texas is worn outdoors, hence a thing that stays on outside.

clue.text: Most thin blood sets in ripples at the edges

indicators.note: at the edges means the rearranged letters sit around the relatives
ripples means disturbs, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: blood means kin, as in blood relations

explanation.surface: Blood gathering in ripples along the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripples' rearranges SETS IN to SNIEST, around KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means thin, so its superlative means thinnest.

clue.text: Good if doing reverse flip to show sign of modesty

indicators.note: doing reverse means the two pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: to leaf through pages is to flip through them

explanation.surface: A gymnastics remark: it's fine if one performs a backward flip.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical art a carved leaf covers nudity, so it symbolises modesty.

clue.text: Like poker? No thanks, I say!

explanation.walkthrough: A poker sits in the grate of a fire; an ungrateful person refuses to say thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person withholds thanks; and a fire poker usually rests in the fireplace.

clue.text: Escape, in glee changing alias

indicators.note: in means the alias goes inside the rearranged letters
changing means altering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: aka, also known as, introduces an alias

explanation.surface: A getaway, gleefully taking on a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escape' looks like a verb but is a noun, as in an escape of gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the escape of fluid or information through a gap.

clue.text: Perform opening turn in Manhattan dance?

parts.note: the United Nations, UN, has its headquarters in Manhattan
the Twist is a 1960s dance

explanation.surface: A question about a dance in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: to untwist is to turn something so that it opens or unwinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwinding a twisted thing means turning it in the reverse direction so it opens out.

clue.text: Game makes you happy with high jump to follow?

parts.note: up means cheerful or happy
to be for the high jump means trouble is coming, the same as being for it

explanation.surface: A sport where you are thrilled to watch a high jump next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the high jump' is British slang for about to be punished, equivalent to 'for it'. 'makes you' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Game as an adjective means willing to have a go, which is the sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Patch up angry local dispute

parts.note: turf is a patch of grass, or one's patch or territory

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: raw can mean sore or angry

explanation.surface: Patching things up after an angry neighbourhood quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf war is a fight over territory, typically between local gangs.

clue.text: Sounded amused that driver should pay?

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as golf: a driver (a club) should pay heed to the peg the ball sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: To titter is to laugh in an amused way; and a golf driver ought to attend to the peg.

clue.text: End argument with this tiebreaker?

parts.note: a goal is an end or aim
a difference is a disagreement or argument

explanation.surface: Proposing a settlement of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with this' is a link. In football league tables, goal difference (goals scored minus conceded) separates teams level on points.
explanation.definitionFit: In football leagues the margin of goals scored over conceded separates teams level on points, so it breaks ties.

clue.text: Two old men, one after Oscar

indicators.note: two means the piece is taken twice

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man

explanation.surface: A pair of elderly fellows, one following a man called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' is slang for father, so each old man is PA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for P comes immediately after Oscar for O.

clue.text: Exceptionally few ultimately in what before could be rife

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the exclamation

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
exceptionally means very, as in exceptionally good

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of the word

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Exceptionally few things in what came before could be widespread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link. 'what' as the exclamation 'eh?' is the hard step.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rife is widespread, found in every place.

clue.text: One of the females within confines of Judges?

definitions.text: One of the females within confines of Judges?

indicators.note: within means the female sheep go inside the outer letters
confines are boundaries, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: A reference to a woman found in the Book of Judges.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also points to the answer: Deborah, a judge in the Book of Judges, was a Hebrew woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a Hebrew woman, such as the figures who appear in the biblical Book of Judges.

clue.text: Done over time, that is valued all round

indicators.note: all round means the abbreviation for that is surrounds the time letter

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is
rated means valued or assessed

explanation.surface: Repeated in time, a thing that is esteemed everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat, so something iterated has been done over again.
